name: Dassault Falcon 50/900/7X/8X
summary: Dassault's three-engine long-range business jets, valued for short-field performance and the ability to overfly oceans with three engines.

wings: Low swept wing; the 7X/8X wing is thinner and more swept
Winglets on the 900LX, 7X and 8X; plain tips on older 50/900s
engines: Three engines: two pods on the rear fuselage plus a third in the tail fed by an intake at the base of the fin
fuselage: Fuselage with a long pointed nose and a row of rounded windows
Falcon 50 is noticeably shorter than the 900/7X/8X
tail: Cruciform tail: horizontal stabilizer mounted partway up the fin, not on top

tellTales: Air intake for a third engine at the base of the fin
Three engine exhausts at the tail
Tailplane set partway up the fin, below the top

confusedWith.howToTell: The trijet has a third engine with an intake at the fin root; the Falcon 2000 has only two engine pods and a clean fin root.
The Falcon trijet has three engines and a mid-fin tailplane; the G650/G700 has two engines and a T-tail.
The Falcon trijet has three engines; the Hawker 800 has two and oval windows.
